lessons.intro: Distinguish population proportion p from sample proportion p-hat. Construct/interpret a simulated distribution whose marks are sample proportions.

lessons.title: Conditions for Sampling a Proportion
lessons.intro: Recognize unbiasedness from a sampling distribution centered at p. Connect random selection/coverage to unbiased center; distinguish bias from smaller variability.

lessons.title: Intro to Confidence Intervals
lessons.intro: Construct an interval as point estimate plus/minus margin of error. Recover point estimate and margin of error from endpoints.

lessons.title: Interval for a Proportion
lessons.intro: Identify population, parameter, sample, statistic, categorical response, and study design. Choose a one-sample z-interval for a population proportion.

lessons.title: Confidence & Margins of Error
lessons.intro: Distinguish standard error from known-population standard deviation. Find and interpret critical z values for different central confidence levels.

lessons.title: Introduction to Hypothesis Tests
lessons.intro: Simulate a null process and estimate one-sided tail evidence from counts. Recognize the role of null assumption and sample-size effect on evidence.

lessons.title: Hypothesis Test for One Proportion
lessons.intro: Set up a one-proportion z-test with contextual parameter/hypotheses. Use the null p0 in the mean, SD, large-count checks, and z denominator.

lessons.title: Errors & Power
lessons.intro: Distinguish flawed design/bias/confounding from chance errors in valid inference. Describe Type I and Type II errors and consequences in context.
